reviews.comment: Great Professor, very responsive to emails and questions. The exams were easy, just use the practice exams to prep. The homeworks are really long, but easy. I rated him a 4 because the TA was not very responsive and I would get homework back the day before or after the exam with insufficient time to review and he gave little to no feedback

As a stat major who struggles with advanced concepts, I LOVED having this class with Professor Raj. He clearly explains concepts, and while homework can be long and tedious, if you make sure you understand the questions and how to solve them, the exams are a breeze. Models exams after homework and practice exams. Would take him again!
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Guhaniyogi is a great professor that makes the class an easy A. He is not a bad lecturer at all but has an accent. Sometimes he will not be as lenient towards deadlines and assignments because he already makes the course super straightforward. All the assignments are open note and exactly like the Cengage homework.
Easy "A" . He really cares about everyone and understands that you don't have to grade stupidly hard for people to learn the material. Great dude.

This prof is amazing! Really easy class with online HW/Exams (open note) and he gives two attempts for each problem. The test questions are the exact same as ones on HW. Not many showed up to his lectures but he knows his stuff and can answer questions really well. He responds to emails quick. If you just do your work you will get the A.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easiest A at TAMU. The class itself is very similar to AP statistics for the most part. Lectures are quite dull though. Many people do not show up to class and still get A's. Tests are exactly like the homework and the reviews are very good.

Easy A for 211, even if you never show up to lecture. Doesn't go over everything from the syllabus, so maybe take someone else if you're actually interested in stats. That being said he is extremely knowledgeable about stats, so he can probably answer any questions you have.

He was amazing in that it was easy to get an A. Tests are open internet and very easy. By the end of the semester only about 10 students out of 100 still showed up to his lectures. He doesn't care a lot about teaching as he was frequently late and ended lectures way early. Don't take him if you're a stats major as he doesn't cover everything.

Prof Raj is amazing. The exams and hw are open notes/open internet. The exams are very similar to the hw, the practice exam, and lecture problems(if one attends). Easiest A I've gotten in a class at A&M
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: hw & exam questions are exactly how he teaches it in lecture. He basically gives you a step-by-step on how to get an A, all you have to do is show up to lecture. super nice prof and answers questions clearly. you do need to purchase the homework subscription.

Only downside is that you have to buy the HW for $25 or smth like that. Other than that, he's the best prof out there. Easiest A I've ever had. Missed a total of 2 questions in the entire course. Lectures were completely dead but if you show up, the HWs will be the easiest thing ever. Tests are online with 2 attempts per Q and exactly like the HWs.

He is a great professor who is gives very good lectures. Showing up to class is a cheat code to get an A bc he explains everything so well. He answers emails very fast and is very helpful with questions before or after class. The tests arent easy but they are open note/internet very similar to his pretests so you wont be surprised on the tests.

One of the nicest professors I have had at A&M. Super helpful with questions inside and outside of class, and genuinely cares about teaching his students. Exams are very similar to the Webassign Homeworks, which are also open note. Pretty straightforward class if you pay attention and take notes.

Had him for Stat 211. He clearly knows the material inside and out and is active in the field (you can find his papers and talks on the web). Explains the material well, especially if you ask questions. Super helpful and accessible in office hours. Open note exams which are similar to WebAssign homework. 10/10 would take again.
